subject: Performance benchmarking review — scheduling and prep
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@edgescale.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2026-05-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Benchmarking review request — load tests and targets

Hi Marissa / Tom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we were really impressed with the throughput and the routing options. Our infra/ML teams asked if we could set up a focused benchmarking/architecture deep-dive to validate production targets before we sign the commitment. High level ask: help us run load tests + review architecture choices (KV cache, batching, quantization) and confirm token throughput and latency at scale.

Target goals (initial ask from EdgeScale):
- Sustained throughput: ~200,000 tokens/minute across the service (peak bursts up to 300k)
- Target RPS equivalence: ~20-30 requests/sec with average response length ~256 tokens (we can adjust)
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 350ms for 32-token responses, p95 <= 800ms for 256-token responses
- Concurrency: simulate 50 concurrent clients (steady-state) with short bursts to 200 concurrent

Ideally we'd like a 60-90 minute session to (1) review the load-test plan, (2) agree on metrics & env, and (3) run a short smoke test. Are you available next week? We have some availability on Tue 6/1 or Wed 6/2 (PST).

I've attached our high-level load test worksheet.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Infrastructure
EdgeScale Inc.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-29T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Benchmarking review request — load tests and targets

Thanks for the ping. Quick notes from infra: we can provision a dedicated test pool for EdgeScale for the session. Proposed config:
- 4 inference workers (N nodes) behind the routing policy to simulate real production routing
- We'll run the harness with variable-length prompts: short (32), medium (128), long (256) tokens; we can tune to the client's distribution
- Target we can reliably aim for in the session: sustained ~150k tokens/min (2.5k tokens/sec) with burst to 300k for short intervals. We should call out that sustained 200k is doable but may require additional workers/parallelism.

Measurement & instrumentation:
- Collect per-token latency, per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and overall throughput.
- Warmup: recommend 10-15 minute KV cache warmup at target QPS before measuring steady-state.

Open questions for the client: whether they want us to test quantized model variants (smaller memory footprint) vs full fp16. Quantized variants typically show lower throughput but huge cost savings; we should document tradeoffs.

I'll attach the RPS/target chart so we can align on the mapping between requests/sec and tokens/min.
